items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The pianist was Glen Buschmann... He and I had a friendly disagreement about a number that I was featuring and he had recently made an arrangement on the number and played it on two of the first concerts we did

ctx.x: The 10th of September, I had to leave Chamonix for Geneva, Switzerland, where I was to take a train for Hannover, Germany to begin the 21 days tour of that country. The concert tour of France was to begin the 13th of October. Lily was to leave for Paris in a few days and would inquire about a drummer to replace Tommy Benford.

The 12th of September, I met the orchestra, rehearsed with them that afternoon and did a concert at the Niedersachsenhalle in Hannover that night. The leader of the orchestra was a trumpet player named Fred Bunge(prounced Bun-gee), Teddy Paris was the name of the drummer and the pianist was Glen Buschmann. There was a sax man, trombone and bass, but I dont remember their names. The group had also a girl singer and another girl that played harmonica, and a master of ceremonies. Fred was considered as the best jazz…

Teddy Paris was an up to date drummer that knew how to push a soloist and he put just as much heart in what he played behind me as he did for those that he had been playing with for a long time. I'd say that he was a German Sid Catlett. And Glen was a fine pianist, sort of in a Teddy Wilson style and an arranger also. He and I had a friendly disagreement about a number that I was featuring and he had recently made an arrangement on the number and played it on two of the first concerts we did, before I came on.…
